newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Serb tells UN court of rape by Bosnian camp guard.
newsitem.headline: Serb tells UN court of rape by Bosnian camp guard.

text.p: A Bosnian Serb woman told the U.N. criminal tribunal for former Yugoslavia on Thursday how amid a climate of fear and desperation she was repeatedly raped at the Celebici prison camp in 1992.
Testifying at the war crimes trial of three Moslems and a Croat, 48-year-old Milojka Antic said she had been rounded up taken to the camp in central Bosnia for no apparent reason in June 1992.
There, one of the Moslem defendants and deputy commander of the camp, Hazim Delic, summoned her to a room and forced her to strip at gunpoint before raping her, she said.

"He ordered me to take my clothes off. I was crying but he threatened me with a rifle and cursed me, I was frightened he would kill me," she said, facing away from the dock, where Delic sat impassively staring ahead.
She said on one occasion Delic had attempted to rape her anally but stopped when her screams of pain became too loud.
"He told me to get on to the bed and to kneel...I screamed because it hurt very much. My anus started to bleed and that's when he turned me over."
Antic said that after such an ordeal she would be returned to the darkened room she shared with other female inmates.
"I was in tears but they could not see them...I said to myself...God, if you exist, why did you not protect me from this," she told the court.
Delic is charged with fellow Moslems Esad "Zenga" Landzo and Zejnil Delalic and Bosnian Croat Zdravko "Pavo" Mucic with the murder, rape and torture of Serb prisoners during the summer of 1992.
Questioned by prosecutor Giuliano Turone, Antic said she had been interrogated on arrival at Celebici by Mucic.
She said that when he discovered she was unmarried Mucic had turned to Delic and said: "This is just the right type for you".
Antic's testimony followed that given in mid-March by her friend Grozdana Cecez, who said she was also raped by Delic.
The Hague trial is the first war crimes hearing since the Tokyo trials after World War Two to deal with accusations of rape and sexual assault.

The tribunal has so far indicted 75 suspects with war crimes -- 54 Serbs (one of whom has since died), 18 Croats and three Moslems. One man, Drazen Erdemovic, has been convicted and sentenced to 10 years in jail. A verdict in another case -- that of Dusan "Dusko" Tadic -- is expected soon.
The two most prominent indicted suspects are former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadic and former Bosnian Serb military commander Radko Mladic, both of whom remain at large.
